market_context: An early-session relief rally sparked by tumbling crude oil has fully reversed as technology and semiconductor stocks resumed their late-October selloff. Broad indexes are pressured by deal-related drops in Marvell and Lumentum, Oracle's stock offering, and institutional de-risking ahead of Apple's post-market earnings and Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections. With the VIX climbing above 20 and markets trading below key dealer gamma levels, tech-heavy benchmarks remain vulnerable to closing-bell distribution.

predictions.reasoning: SPY surrendered an intraday gain of over 1.1% to turn negative by mid-afternoon as tech weakness offset gains in defensive and industrial sectors. With the VIX rising 6.6% to 20.71 and the tape operating in negative gamma territory, late-day index rebalancing into midterm election risk is poised to pull SPY down toward its session low near $753.11.

The Nasdaq-100 ETF experienced a sharp intraday reversal from highs near $699.43, weighed down by steep declines in Oracle (-8.5%) and Marvell (-13%) alongside general AI capex skepticism. Heavy institutional de-risking in large-cap hardware and software ahead of Apple's earnings will keep persistent downward pressure on QQQ into the 4:00 PM close.

Apple is hovering just above its intraday low of $335.84 as investors trim exposure ahead of its fiscal Q4 earnings report scheduled for 4:30 PM ET. Trader caution remains elevated after last quarter's beat still triggered a 7.4% next-day drop, leading options traders and fund managers to hedge rather than buy into the closing bell.

Microsoft is trading near its daily low of $512.41 as the cloud sector continues to absorb negative sentiment surrounding elevated capital expenditures and free cash flow dilution. Persistent afternoon selling across mega-cap tech leaves little bid support in the final 45 minutes of the session.
